question: John 3:16 tells us that God loved the world so much He gave His only Son. When did you last feel deeply loved by God — and how did that experience change the way you loved others?

Psalm 23 paints a picture of a shepherd who provides rest, guidance, and comfort through the darkest valleys. What is a 'dark valley' you've walked through recently, and how did you sense God's presence with you?

Philippians 4:13 reminds us that strength comes through Christ, not from ourselves. Is there a challenge you've been trying to push through on your own? What would it look like to lean on God's strength instead?
Romans 8:28 promises that God works all things together for good — even the painful ones. Can you think of a hard season in your life that, looking back, you can see God's hand working for your good?

Proverbs 3:5 calls us to trust God rather than our own understanding. Is there a decision or uncertainty in your life right now where you're tempted to figure everything out yourself? What does trusting God look like in that situation?
Isaiah 40:31 says those who wait on the Lord will renew their strength. Waiting is hard. What are you currently waiting on God for, and how are you staying hopeful in that season of waiting?

Matthew 6:33 invites us to seek God's kingdom first and trust that everything else will follow. What is one area of your life where you've been putting other things before God — and what would it look like to reorder your priorities?
Psalm 46:1 calls God a 'very present help in trouble.' When was the last time you ran to God in a crisis rather than trying to handle it alone? How did His presence make a difference?
Romans 15:13 speaks of being filled with hope, joy, and peace through trusting God. Which of those three — hope, joy, or peace — do you feel most in need of right now, and why?
Joshua 1:9 reminds us that courage doesn't mean the absence of fear — it means moving forward knowing God is with us. What is one thing you've been afraid to do that God might be calling you toward?
Lamentations 3:22-23 says God's mercies are new every morning. When did you last wake up and genuinely thank God for a fresh start? What would change if you began each day expecting new mercy?
Jeremiah 29:11 promises that God has plans for hope and a future — but those plans often require waiting and trust. How do you stay faithful when God's plan seems slow or unclear?
Matthew 11:28 is Jesus' personal invitation: 'Come to Me, and I will give you rest.' What burdens are you carrying right now that you haven't fully handed over to Jesus? What makes it hard to let go?

Ephesians 2:8-9 tells us that salvation is a gift — not something we earn. Do you ever find yourself trying to earn God's love through good behavior? How does remembering grace change how you see yourself?

1 Corinthians 13 defines love through actions — patience, kindness, not keeping score. Who in your life is it hardest to love that way? What would one small act of love toward them look like this week?
Psalm 139:14 says you are fearfully and wonderfully made. What part of yourself do you struggle to see as 'wonderful'? How might God see that part of you differently than you do?

2 Timothy 1:7 says God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and a sound mind. What fear has been holding you back lately — and what would it look like to step into the power God has given you?
Romans 10:9 connects confession and belief as the path to salvation. Is there something you know in your head about God that you haven't fully believed in your heart? What's the gap between the two?

Jesus said in John 14:6, 'I am the way, the truth, and the life.' In a world full of competing voices telling you how to live, how do you filter what's true? How has Jesus' truth shaped the way you make decisions?

Psalm 119:105 compares God's Word to a lamp — it lights the very next step, not the whole path. When was the last time Scripture specifically guided you in a real-life situation? What did you do with that guidance?

Galatians 5:22-23 lists the fruit of the Spirit — love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Which fruit feels most lacking in your life right now, and what do you think that's telling you about your connection with God?

1 Peter 5:7 says to cast all your anxiety on God because He cares for you. What worry have you been holding onto that you keep taking back after you've given it to God? What does trusting Him with it fully look like for you?

Romans 12:2 talks about being transformed by the renewing of your mind. What is one thought pattern or way of thinking you want God to transform this season — and what habit or practice might help that transformation happen?

Jesus said in Matthew 5:14, 'You are the light of the world.' You already are light — the calling is to let it shine. Where in your everyday life (work, home, your neighborhood) do you have an opportunity to shine right now?
Isaiah 41:10 stacks four promises on top of each other: I am with you, I am your God, I will strengthen you, I will help you. Which of those four do you need most today, and why?

Colossians 3:23 says to do your work 'heartily, as to the Lord.' Think about what you did today — your job, your chores, caring for someone. What would it look like to do that same thing tomorrow as an act of worship?

Psalm 37:4 says, 'Delight yourself in the Lord, and He will give you the desires of your heart.' What does delighting in God actually look like in your daily life — not just on Sunday, but on a regular Tuesday?

2 Chronicles 7:14 says healing begins when God's people humble themselves and pray. Is there a situation — in your family, community, or the world — that you feel burdened to pray for? What would it look like to actually commit to praying for it?

John 16:33 says, 'In this world you will have trouble. But take heart — I have overcome the world.' Where in your life right now do you need to hear that Jesus has already overcome? How does His victory change how you face what you're going through?

Revelation 21:4 promises a day when God wipes away every tear and makes all things new. When you think about that promise, what brings you the most comfort — and how does the hope of what's coming change how you live today?
